planting.note: Direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost, or in late summer for a fall and winter crop in zone 9; unlike true spinach, this leaf beet resists bolting through summer heat while still tasting spinach-like.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Perpetual Spinach is an old English strain of leaf beet grown specifically as a heat- and bolt-resistant substitute for true spinach, with smaller, smoother, thinner-stalked leaves than standard Swiss chard and a milder, more spinach-like flavor when cooked. Unlike true spinach, which bolts quickly in warm weather, this leaf beet keeps producing tender new leaves through much of the growing season, giving gardeners a reliable spinach-flavored green across a far longer window. Harvest outer leaves continuously as needed, leaving the growing center intact, and expect the plant to keep cropping for months with regular cutting.

planting.note: Direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost, or in late summer for a fall and winter crop in zone 9; the candy-striped stalks are most vivid when cut young for salad use.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Peppermint chard produces glossy, savoyed green leaves on stalks striped in bands of pink and white, resembling the candy for which it is named and giving it strong visual appeal both in the garden and sliced into salads. Flavor is typical of Swiss chard, with tender leaves that cook down like spinach and crisp stalks that can be prepared like celery, and the coloring holds reasonably well when lightly cooked. Harvest outer leaves regularly as needed to keep the plant productive, and expect continued cropping over a long cool-season harvest window with cut-and-come-again picking.

common_name: Pink Passion Chard (Vivid Hot Pink Stem Chard)

planting.note: Direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost, or in late summer for a fall and winter crop in zone 9; Pink Passion holds its bright stem color well through the cool season.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Pink Passion is a modern chard cultivar bred for exceptionally vivid, saturated hot-pink stalks and midribs that stand out strongly against dark, glossy, savoyed green leaves, making it a favorite for ornamental edible plantings as well as the kitchen. Both leaves and stalks are edible with classic chard flavor, the leaves cooking down like spinach and the crisp, colorful stalks holding their hue reasonably well when sautéed or roasted. Harvest outer leaves continuously as needed, leaving the growing center intact, and expect strong production through the cool season with regular cutting.
